cells.speakerNotes:
KEY MESSAGE
This is a stakeholder question, not a dashboard request — and the answer runs through tested models, not a spreadsheet.

SAY
"Kari asked: when storms hit, do the lasers slow down? Over the next 20 minutes I'll show how I turned that into metrics I can trust, a tested dbt model that answers it, and what two weeks of data honestly supports."
"The scope is deliberately small and honest: two sites analysed, five pens compared, three storm episodes. Enough to build and validate the method — not enough to claim causation."
"The pipeline line is the architecture in one breath: raw data goes in, tested models come out, decisions come from the marts. DuckDB is the local analytical warehouse where this case is built and tested. dbt owns the transformations, the modelling and the tests. Snowflake is the intended production platform — not the warehouse running this case. Power BI is how stakeholders like Kari consume it."
"Every analytical figure is queried live from the DuckDB marts."

TECHNICAL DETAILS
- 2 sites, 5 pens, 63 pen-days, 3 episodes, 6 site-days with storm exposure; window 1–14 October 2026, source-driven, no CURRENT_DATE.
- The case is implemented and tested on DuckDB. Snowflake is the target production platform, not the running warehouse.
- The deck reads main_marts and main_intermediate read-only; dbt build must run first.

TRANSITION
"Let me start with what the farmers actually report."

KEY MESSAGE
A decline in total shots cannot tell us why activity dropped — the analysis has to separate three explanations first.

SAY
"Farmers report that the lasers seem less active after storms. But a decline in total shots alone cannot tell us why. Three explanations fit the same observation."
"One: reduced availability — the node operates for fewer hours, so total shots fall with it. Two: reduced activity while operating — the node is running, but fires fewer shots per operating hour. Three: changed detection conditions — fish behaviour or rough-water conditions may change what the camera detects and, with it, the firing demand. That third one is a hypothesis to investigate, not something this data can prove."
"The analysis will answer three questions: does activity change during storms, are some pens or sites more affected, and does activity recover afterwards. Each uses the same daily model, so the answers are comparable."
"The output has to support a customer conversation, an inspection priority, and a decision about what the team instruments next."

TECHNICAL DETAILS
- Availability is proxied by uptime minutes; behaviour by shots per operating hour; both are defined on the metric slide, not here.
- The detection-conditions explanation stays a hypothesis: the extract has no fish-behaviour or water-condition measurements.
- There is no site name or geography in the extract, so the deck keeps S01/S02 and P101…P202.

TRANSITION
"Here is the data we actually have to answer it."

KEY MESSAGE
Four sources, four levels of detail — the hard part is getting their timing aligned.

SAY
"Four files, 80 rows in total. Each one tells us something different. Node activity gives us daily shots, lice detections and operating time per laser node. Node assignments tell us which site and pen each node belonged to, and when — that is how we track movements and credit activity to the right pen."
"Storm events tell us when and where storms happened and how severe they were; we turn each storm into the minutes it affected each local day. Farmer logs are manual fish counts, which we use as population context — the latest plausible count."
"Before comparing anything, I align all four sources to the same local calendar day. The shared view is one row per site, pen and day: 63 pen-days."
"Some pen-days have incomplete equipment records — two of the 63. I keep those missing values separate from a reported zero, so missing data is never mistaken for a machine that stopped."

TECHNICAL DETAILS
- Grains: node × day (61 rows), node × interval (6), storm × site with UTC timestamps (3), pen × entry with naive local timestamps (10).
- Storms are split into local-day exposure using DST-aware day boundaries; the extract sits before the Oslo fall-back, so all days are 1,440 minutes.
- node_daily_activity has no site or pen; the effective-dated assignment is the temporal bridge.
- Incomplete pen-days: N05 on its 8 Oct move day, N04 on 12 Oct; measures stay null and has_activity_record = false.

TRANSITION
"Small data, but it fights back in three specific places."

KEY MESSAGE
Each raw-data problem has a clear practical consequence — and a specific modelling decision.

SAY
"First, a node changes pens. N05 moved from P202 at S02 to P103 at S01 on 8 October, and there is no activity record for the day it moved. If I linked activity to a node without considering when it moved, I could credit its activity to the wrong pen. So I use the assignment valid on each date: the move day belongs to the new pen, and its missing activity stays missing."
"Second, a missing record is not zero activity. N05 and N04 have days with no record, while N01 and N03 explicitly report zero operating time on other days. Treating both as zero would distort the comparison — no record may mean the equipment was inactive, or that the record never arrived. I build an expected record for every node and day it should be assigned, so I can tell missing data from a reported zero."
"Third, farmer-entered counts need checking. P102 has two entries on 8 October, including a correction, and P201 reports 1,852,000 fish, which is implausible. Duplicates or bad counts would distort the population picture. I keep the original entries, use the latest valid count, and flag implausible values rather than silently replacing them."
"Each of those decisions is enforced as a validation rule and a test in dbt."

TECHNICAL DETAILS
- Assignment intervals are half-open [valid_from, valid_until); valid_to is inclusive in the source, so staging adds one day. The effective-dated join attributes one node-day to exactly one assignment.
- The node-day spine keeps has_activity_record; missing measures stay NULL, while a reported zero keeps 0 uptime and a null rate.
- Duplicate resolution is deterministic: latest logged_at_local, then highest log_id. Implausible entries (above fish_count_plausible_max) are flagged and withheld, with the source log id and timestamp retained.
- 10 unit tests cover the move day, the correction, the timestamp tie, implausibility and staleness; singular tests cover the storm and snapshot guards.

TRANSITION
"Those decisions define the metric."

KEY MESSAGE
Four metrics separate availability, detection activity, firing activity and firing per detection — a fall in shots alone cannot tell us which changed.

SAY
"Raw shots compare the wrong thing across pens with different operating time. I use four metrics. Uptime % tells us how much of the expected operating time the equipment was actually running. Detections per uptime hour tells us how often lice were detected while it ran. Shots per uptime hour tells us how actively the laser fired while it ran. And shots per detection relates firing to what was detected."
"All four are ratios of totals: total minutes, total detections, total shots. I never average daily or per-node rates — that gives every day equal weight and silently drops zero-uptime days."
"Uptime % uses expected operating minutes as the denominator: assigned nodes × the true local day length, so 23- and 25-hour DST days are handled correctly. Uptime is reported node on-time, not proof the laser was armed. When a denominator is missing or zero, the rate is NULL — never zero."
"Read the four together. If uptime falls, investigate power, connectivity or shutdowns. If detections per hour fall, investigate detection conditions, fish behaviour or lice prevalence. If shots per hour fall, investigate firing activity and operating logic. If shots per detection changes, investigate how firing relates to detections. These are possible explanations to investigate, not established causes."
"Reporting completeness sits alongside the metrics — 61 of 63 node-days here — so a comparison is never read without its reliability. Fish counts give population context but are never a denominator. And a detection does not automatically mean a shot; the firing logic needs confirmation."

TECHNICAL DETAILS
- uptime_pct = uptime_minutes / expected_node_minutes × 100; expected_node_minutes = expected_node_days × day_duration_minutes (DST-aware: 1380/1440/1500).
- detections_per_operating_hour = lice_detection_count / uptime_minutes × 60; shots_per_operating_hour = laser_shot_count / uptime_minutes × 60; shots_per_detection = laser_shot_count / lice_detection_count.
- All rates are ratios of summed totals over the comparison window; daily or per-node rates are never averaged. NULL when the denominator is zero or missing.
- Reporting completeness = reported_node_days / expected_node_days (61/63 = 96.8%).
- 'Operating hour' in the charts means uptime hour: reported node on-time, not calendar time.
- Fish counts are semi-additive snapshots used for context only. Detections and shots are not assumed to be 1:1; the firing logic needs confirmation.

TRANSITION
"Now how the pipeline is engineered to make those metrics trustworthy."

KEY MESSAGE
Clear layer boundaries, explicit analytical grain and tested business logic are what make the models reliable and reusable.

SAY
"Staging is deliberately boring: four views, one per source, doing only renaming, casting and timestamp normalisation. It stays 1:1 with the source, so problems are easy to trace."
"Intermediate is where the business logic lives: temporal joins, validation and aggregation. The marts then expose business-ready facts and dimensions — no logic hidden in the reports."
"There are two fact grains because there are two questions. The daily fact is one row per site, pen and day, and it is the additive source for overall totals. The storm-window fact is one row per pen, episode and day, for before/during/after comparisons. Keeping them separate prevents misleading totals and double counting."
"Reliability comes from tests. The project has 356 tests, including 10 unit tests for edge cases like the node move day and fish-count corrections. The decisions you would normally put in a SQL slide — half-open assignment intervals, DST-aware storm exposure and missing-versus-zero handling — are implemented and tested in the models."
"This slide is about how the pipeline is organised; the raw-data problems themselves were covered in the data-quality slide."

TECHNICAL DETAILS
- 19 models: 4 staging views, 9 intermediate models, 6 mart tables; four raw CSV sources.
- Staging views are 1:1 with sources; intermediate models are views; marts are tables.
- Tests: 356 total (346 data/singular + 10 unit), 355 pass, 1 intentional warn.
- Examples of tested rules: N05's effective-dated assignment, the 300/1,440/420 storm split across local days, missing activity kept NULL, fish-count plausibility and staleness.
- Built and tested on DuckDB; Snowflake is the intended production platform. Portability notes: docs/production_portability.md.

TRANSITION
"Now the dimensional model that exposes those two grains."

KEY MESSAGE
Two fact tables because there are two questions: how each pen performs over time, and how activity compares around a specific storm episode.

SAY
"The daily activity fact is one row per site, pen and day: 63 rows. It carries shots, lice detections, operating time, reporting completeness and fish-count context. It is the additive operational source of truth — when Kari wants overall totals, this is the table."
"The storm-window fact is one row per pen, storm episode and day: 39 rows, but only 36 unique pen-days. It adds the before/during/after classification and the actual storm exposure, so we can compare activity around a particular episode."
"The two facts share the date, site and pen dimensions. The storm episode dimension joins only the storm-window fact. There is deliberately no fact-to-fact join."
"The warning matters: because three pen-days appear in two episode windows, summing the storm-window fact across episodes would double-count 1,299 shots. Use the daily fact for overall totals."
"Fish counts live on the daily fact only; join on pen and date when you need population context in the window analysis."

TECHNICAL DETAILS
- fct_pen_daily_activity: 63 rows; grain site × pen × date; built from int_pen_daily_activity, int_pen_daily_fish_count and int_site_daily_storm_summary.
- fct_pen_storm_window_day: 39 rows / 36 unique pen-days; grain pen × episode × date; built from int_pen_storm_daily_analysis.
- Dimensions: dim_date, dim_site and dim_pen join both facts; dim_storm_episode joins only the storm-window fact.
- Storm exposure (storm_minutes, storm_count, has_storm) is a site-day value repeated per pen; never sum across pens.
- The three duplicated pen-days sit in two episode windows; summing the window fact double-counts 1,299 shots.
- Built and tested on DuckDB; Snowflake is the intended production platform; docs/production_portability.md lists the engine-specific constructs.

TRANSITION
"Now what the data shows."

KEY MESSAGE
The lineage is four sources -> staging -> intermediate -> marts, with the business logic concentrated in intermediate models.

SAY
"Everything starts from four sources with different grains: node activity is node-day, assignments are deployment intervals, storms are UTC events per site, and farmer logs are manual pen entries. Staging only standardises them - rename, cast, normalise timestamps - and keeps the source grain, so no business logic is buried there."

"The interesting work is in intermediate. int_node_days_assigned applies the assignment valid on each date and builds an expected node-day spine, so missing telemetry stays null instead of becoming zero. int_pen_daily_activity aggregates those node-days to pen-day and defines the shared metrics. In parallel, int_dates gives us the DST-aware local day, while int_storm_daily_exposure splits storms across local days and int_storm_episodes groups them. int_pen_storm_daily_analysis then classifies each pen-day as before, during or after."

"That produces two facts: the daily fact for overall totals, combining activity, fish-count snapshots and site-day exposure; and the storm-window fact for event comparisons. The dimensions come off the same upstream models and filter both facts consistently. The facts are never joined directly, which avoids duplicating pen-days. And because every edge is a dbt ref(), the manifest lets us trace any dashboard number back to its source."

TECHNICAL DETAILS
- Sources: node_daily_activity, node_pen_assignment, storm_events, farmer_pen_log. Staging models are views and stay 1:1 with the extracts.
- Staging: stg_stingray__node_daily_activity, stg_stingray__node_pen_assignments, stg_stingray__storm_events, stg_stingray__farmer_pen_logs.
- Intermediate (all views): int_dates, int_node_days_assigned, int_fish_counts_validated, int_pen_daily_fish_count, int_storm_episodes, int_storm_daily_exposure, int_site_daily_storm_summary, int_pen_daily_activity, int_pen_storm_daily_analysis.
- fct_pen_daily_activity <- int_pen_daily_activity + int_pen_daily_fish_count + int_site_daily_storm_summary.
- fct_pen_storm_window_day <- int_pen_storm_daily_analysis.
- dim_date <- int_dates; dim_site <- stg_stingray__node_pen_assignments + stg_stingray__storm_events; dim_pen <- stg_stingray__node_pen_assignments + int_fish_counts_validated; dim_storm_episode <- int_storm_episodes.
- dim_date, dim_site and dim_pen join both facts; dim_storm_episode joins the storm-window fact only.
- No fact-to-fact join. Marts are tables; staging and intermediate models are views.
- Every displayed edge was checked against target/manifest.json parent_map; no invented models or dependencies.

TRANSITION
"So what does that lineage actually show in the data?"

KEY MESSAGE
S01's high-severity storm coincided with lower firing rates in all three pens — but the underlying changes were different.

SAY
"Start with the main finding: against each pen's own three quiet days, weighted shots per uptime hour fell 24% for P101, 49% for P102 and 8% for P103."
"The reasons differ. P102 is the cleanest behavioural signal: reported operating time barely moved (+0.3%), but the firing rate halved while the laser was running. For P101 and P103, operating hours fell 54% and 76%, and total shots fell 65% and 78% — that is largely an availability story, not a firing-behaviour story."
"Read the caveats with the numbers. P103's after-window is only 67% complete because of the 8 October node reassignment, so its recovery is the least certain. S02 is much quieter: P201 +2.6% during the moderate episode and -3.3% during the low one. And there is one high-severity episode, so this is co-movement, not causation."
"Completeness is strong where it matters for this comparison — 100% before and during for all three S01 pens — but the after-period for P103 is thinner. Uptime is reported node on-time, not proof the laser was armed."

TECHNICAL DETAILS
- Rates are total shots ÷ total operating minutes × 60, from summed totals over each period — never an average of daily rates.
- Changes compare each pen's during window with its own three quiet days before the S01 high-severity episode.
- Completeness = reported ÷ expected node-days. S01 before/during is 100% for all three pens; P103 after is 66.7%.
- S02 values: P201 +2.6% during the moderate episode, -3.3% during the low episode.
- One high-severity episode: descriptive only, no control for season, biomass or node changes.

TRANSITION
"How would Kari use this without me in the room?"

KEY MESSAGE
Every dashboard visual is traceable to a tested dbt mart: two facts for two questions, sharing three conformed dimensions.

SAY
"This is the Power BI concept, and each visual now has a small label showing its source. The four KPI cards and the daily timeline use fct_pen_daily_activity, the daily operational fact - one row per site, pen and date. The timeline also uses dim_date and dim_pen, with storm bands from dim_storm_episode. This fact is the source of truth for overall totals, because each pen-day appears exactly once."

"The before/during/after chart answers a different question, so it uses fct_pen_storm_window_day with dim_storm_episode and dim_pen. Each row is a pen, episode and day inside the window - the right grain for event comparisons. Fish-count context is not a separate mart; it comes from the fish_count snapshot on the daily fact. Site and pen filters use the shared dimensions."

"Both facts join dim_date, dim_site and dim_pen, so filters stay consistent. They are deliberately not joined to each other: a pen-day can appear in more than one episode window, so a fact-to-fact join would duplicate records and inflate additive measures. Storm exposure is also site-level and repeated across pens, so never sum it across pens."

TECHNICAL DETAILS
- KPI cards and daily timeline: fct_pen_daily_activity. KPI totals are recomputed from the fact, never hardcoded.
- Timeline: fct_pen_daily_activity + dim_date + dim_pen; coral storm bands from dim_storm_episode.
- Before/during/after: fct_pen_storm_window_day + dim_storm_episode + dim_pen.
- Site and pen filters: dim_site and dim_pen, shared by both facts.
- Fish-count context: fish_count, has_fish_count, fish_count_age_days and fish_count_log_id on fct_pen_daily_activity. There is no separate fish-count mart; int_pen_daily_fish_count is the intermediate model behind those columns.
- Missing telemetry card: int_node_days_assigned. Missing measures stay null, never zero.
- Shared dimensions: dim_date, dim_site, dim_pen. dim_storm_episode joins only fct_pen_storm_window_day.
- No fact-to-fact join. The 39 storm-window rows map to 36 unique pen-days; summing across episodes double-counts 1,299 shots, so overall totals come from the daily fact.
- Storm exposure (has_storm, storm_count, storm_minutes, max_storm_severity) is a site-day value repeated per pen and is not additive across pens.

TRANSITION
"What still needs checking before this goes to a customer?

KEY MESSAGE
The transformations are tested; the remaining risk is in source assumptions and production readiness, not hidden logic.

SAY
"Four kinds of checks protect the model: schema and integrity (keys, nulls, relationships); grain and business rules (fact grains, assignment validity, no duplicate pen-days per episode); temporal logic (effective-dated assignments, local-day storms, DST boundaries, episode edges); and calculation and data quality (missing vs zero, NULL rates, fish plausibility, duplicate resolution, staleness)."
"Generic and singular tests run against the real model data; unit tests pin controlled edge cases — for time logic, you can construct the exact move day or DST boundary and assert the output. Two examples: N05's 8 October reassignment applies the new pen but keeps missing telemetry missing. ST-0041's 36-hour storm splits into 300, 1,440 and 420 minutes across three Oslo days. The P201 1,852,000 count is flagged by a warn test, not corrected or removed."
"Two staging shortcuts have since been addressed: fish-count deduplication and the node-day spine are built in the intermediate layer. What remains is mostly source and deployment: one timezone and an inferred activity-day boundary; a reporting window that ends at the last observation; DST ambiguity in the repeated autumn hour; DuckDB-only testing; and no freshness, contracts or incremental models."
"The next steps follow in order: a site-to-timezone lookup and confirmed day semantics; a declared reporting end; intraday telemetry plus device status; more storm episodes before inference; then Snowflake validation and monitoring."
"The results stay descriptive — co-movement, not causation."

TECHNICAL DETAILS
- Latest verified build (run against a temporary DuckDB copy because the local warehouse was locked): 19 models, 356 tests = 346 data/singular + 10 unit; 355 pass, 1 intentional warn (P201 1,852,000), 0 errors.
- Validation categories: schema/integrity (unique, not-null, relationships); grain/business rules (fact grains, assignment validity, no duplicate pen-days in an episode); temporal logic (effective dating, storm minutes per local day, DST boundaries, episode edges); calculation/data quality (missing vs zero, NULL rates, plausible fish counts, deterministic duplicates, staleness).
- Concrete checks: N05 move-day unit test; ST-0041 300/1,440/420 split; fish-count plausibility and staleness; duplicate tie-break (latest logged_at_local, then highest log_id); FK/orphan checks.
- limitations.md priority: 1 timezone, 2 activity-date boundary, 9 end-of-period visibility, 8 runtime portability, 7 source monitoring; 5 DST ambiguity (notes only). Items 3 and 4 (staging dedup, missing rows) are addressed in int_fish_counts_validated, int_pen_daily_fish_count and int_node_days_assigned.
- Next-step order: source semantics → window completeness → operational telemetry/device status → more storms for inference → Snowflake plus contracts/freshness/incremental.
- The model is not production-ready; the findings are descriptive, not causal.

TRANSITION
"Thank you — questions welcome."
